summary: Move one-shot snapshot restore consumption to the actual eval admission point. Oversized or otherwise host-preflight-rejected evals no longer clear restoreSnapshot or write chunked restore frames; restore chunks are built and wire-checked first, then restore state is committed only after the cell remains the admitted pending cell.

pointers: commit one-shot restore after pending admission
Issue#64: rejected oversized eval does not consume pending snapshot restore

steps: Used the issue's independent AUDIT-07 real-runtime RED as the regression authority: valid checkpoint -> kernel loss -> oversized host-rejected eval -> next valid eval previously lost keep=41.
Replaced side-effecting sendRestoreChunks with buildRestoreFrames so chunked restore data can be read and every frame wire-checked without writing to the kernel pipe.

In evalCell, captured restorePending without mutation, completed restore/eval frame construction and full eval wire preflight, installed the pending cell and caller cancellation, then consumed restoreSnapshot and emitted restore frames only if that exact cell was still admitted.
Added the issue's oversize->valid recovery scenario to the existing full runtime test file through a semantic-anchor guarded one-shot patch; the temporary workflow removed itself after commit.

evidence.note: Existing independent RED on the audited baseline reproduced loss of pending restore after a 300000-character host-rejected eval.
Semantic-anchor patch located the original side-effecting restore helper/preflight/send boundary, applied the minimal admission fix plus regression, committed, and removed the temporary workflow.
Final dual-OS verification is pending on the PR Candidate.

limitations: Chunk payload encoding remains the existing UTF-8 string transport; #82 owns code-point-safe transport.
Danger-full-access launch/cwd representation remains #87; this patch preserves the current chunked-selection rule until that issue explicitly separates cwd from confinement.
